youtube.title: Einstein Never Failed Math. Here's Where the Myth Came From
youtube.description:
In 1935, a rabbi in Princeton showed Albert Einstein a Ripley's Believe It or Not clipping headlined "Greatest living mathematician failed in mathematics." Einstein laughed: he had never failed in mathematics, and had mastered differential and integral calculus before he was fifteen. The real failure: at 16, about two years younger than other applicants, he failed the overall entrance exam for the Swiss Federal Polytechnic in Zurich despite strong math and physics results. His 1896 final certificate from the cantonal school in Aarau shows the top grade, 6, in algebra and geometry.

📂 Case File #058: Einstein's Math
